summary: The UNESCO/People's Republic of China (Great Wall) Co-Sponsored Fellowships are paid for jointly by the Government of China and UNESCO. For 2026-2027 there are 75 fellowships in total, of which 27 are open to new candidates from 135 invited developing Member States. Fellows study at selected Chinese universities, either as a one-year visiting scholar or for a master's or doctoral degree of 2 to 5 years, in English or Chinese depending on the programme. Candidates cannot apply to UNESCO directly: they apply through the National Commission for UNESCO of their country.
eligibility_notes:
Only nationals of the 135 invited Member States can apply (46 in Africa, 38 in Asia and the Pacific, 13 Arab States, 26 in Latin America and the Caribbean, 12 in Europe). Women, and candidates from Africa and Small Island Developing States, especially from least developed countries, are strongly encouraged to apply.

General Visiting Scholar: under 45, at least a senior secondary diploma. Senior Visiting Scholar: under 50, a master's degree or an associate professor position or above. Master's: under 35, a bachelor's degree. Doctoral: under 40, a master's degree. Bachelor's degree study is not offered; prospective graduates may apply with official proof of student status.

Language: proficiency in English for English-taught programmes; for Chinese-taught programmes, HSK Level 3 (visiting scholars) or HSK Level 4 (master's and doctoral). Candidates must also meet the host university's own admission rules for academic ability, language and other criteria, and be in good mental and physical health.

Passport: an ordinary passport valid beyond 1 September 2027 (the guidelines say to renew a passport that has under 12 months left from the expected start; a service or diplomatic passport is not accepted on the programme page). A repeated fellowship under the same UNESCO programme is not allowed, and fellowships cannot be extended or renewed under it.
age_experience_notes: Age at the time of the call: General Visiting Scholar under 45, Senior Visiting Scholar under 50, master's under 35, doctoral under 40. Senior scholars must hold a master's degree or be an associate professor or above. No other work experience is required.
funding_summary: The Chinese Government gives a tuition waiver, a monthly living allowance, on-campus accommodation or an accommodation subsidy, and comprehensive medical insurance. UNESCO adds international travel to and from China at the start and end of the fellowship, a monthly pocket allowance of USD 80 and a termination allowance for excess luggage on return. No allowance is paid for a spouse or dependants, and neither side pays for passport or visa costs. Visiting scholars study for one year; degree students study for 2 to 5 years as the programme requires. The 2026-2027 academic year ends on 15 July 2027.
programmes_note: Fellowships cover study at undergraduate and postgraduate level in education, culture, communication, science and technology (general wording of the guidelines), but bachelor's degree study is not available; a General Visiting Scholar needs only a senior secondary diploma and studies for one year without a degree. Programmes are taught in English or Chinese depending on what each selected university offers. The guidelines send candidates to the China Scholarship Council university list for the available fields; that list could not be read.
institutions_note: Fellowships are tenable at a selected number of Chinese universities. The guidelines name none and point to the China Scholarship Council website for the list of universities and fields. The selection is made by the Chinese universities concerned and approved by the Chinese authorities and UNESCO.

summary.detail: Master's degree of 2 to 5 years (duration stated jointly with doctoral study), full-time at a selected Chinese university, taught in English or Chinese. Entry: bachelor's degree, under 35. Chinese-taught programmes need HSK Level 4; English-taught need English proficiency. Living allowance CNY 3,000 per month.

Doctoral degree of 2 to 5 years (duration stated jointly with master's), full-time at a selected Chinese university, taught in English or Chinese. Entry: master's degree, under 40. Chinese-taught programmes need HSK Level 4; English-taught need English proficiency. Living allowance CNY 3,500 per month.

One-year non-degree Visiting Scholar programme, in two forms: General Visiting Scholar (under 45, senior secondary diploma) and Senior Visiting Scholar (under 50, master's degree or associate professor or above). Research with periodic guidance from an assigned supervisor. Chinese-taught programmes need HSK Level 3. Living allowance CNY 3,000 per month (general) or CNY 3,500 per month (senior). Study plan of at least 500 words.
summary.source_text: one-year Visiting Scholar Programme (as General or Senior scholar)

benefits.limit_text: Tuition waiver for the programme the fellow is enrolled in (Government of China)
benefits.conditions: Applies within the framework of the fellowship programme.

benefits.limit_text: CNY 3,000 per month for General Visiting Scholars and master's students; CNY 3,500 per month for Senior Visiting Scholars and doctoral students (Government of China)
benefits.conditions: Meant to cover meals and other living expenses.

benefits.limit_text: On-campus dormitory (usually a twin-room dormitory) or an accommodation subsidy (Government of China)
benefits.conditions: Fellows required to live on campus get the dormitory; those not required to live on campus get the subsidy. No lodging allowance for a spouse or dependants.

benefits.limit_text: Comprehensive Medical Insurance and Protection Scheme for International Students in China (Government of China)
benefits.conditions: Fellows pay medical expenses below the insurance rebate threshold themselves.

benefits.limit_text: International travel to and from China at the beginning and at the end of the fellowship (UNESCO)
UNESCO monthly pocket allowance of USD 80 and a termination allowance to cover excess luggage charges on return home
benefits.conditions: No allowance for a spouse or dependants from UNESCO or China.
Neither UNESCO nor the Government of China pays them; fellows obtain their own visa from the Chinese embassy or consulate before leaving.

requirements.text: Application Form for the Chinese Government Scholarship in English, completed and submitted online (Type A Application, agency number 00001) in the Chinese Government Scholarship Information System; it can be downloaded and printed afterwards.
Clear scan of the ordinary passport information page, with validity later than 1 September 2027. A passport with under 12 months of validity from the expected start should be renewed first.
Notarised photocopy of the highest diploma; documents not in Chinese or English need a notarised Chinese or English translation.
requirements.conditional_rule: Prospective graduates send official proof of student status from their institution instead

requirements.text: Academic transcripts; a transcript not in Chinese or English needs a notarised Chinese or English translation.

English-taught programmes: an international English test certificate such as IELTS or TOEFL; if none, a UNESCO Certificate of Language Knowledge (Annex IV) signed and stamped by a certified language institution or tutor. Chinese-taught programmes: valid HSK score reports meeting the programme's level.
Pre-admission document from a designated Chinese university: a pre-admission notice from its international students' admission department, or an invitation letter from the university or a professor.
Study plan or research proposal in Chinese or English: at least 500 words for one-year visiting scholar programmes and at least 800 words for postgraduate degree programmes.
Two recommendation letters in Chinese or English from professors or associate professors who know the candidate's work or studies.
requirements.conditional_rule: Postgraduate degree and Senior Visiting Scholar applicants

requirements.text: Photocopy of the Foreigner Physical Examination Form (Annex III) in English, covering all items, signed by the physician, stamped by the hospital and with a sealed photograph; valid 6 months. Keep the original.
Non-criminal record certificate issued by a local public security authority within 6 months of the submission deadline.
Own works uploaded under the 'Example of Art / Other Supporting Documents' heading in the system.
requirements.conditional_rule: Applicants in art- or design-related fields (optional)

requirements.text: Valid documents of a legal guardian in China.
Letter of nomination from the National Commission for UNESCO, sent to UNESCO with the application form and all documents.

application_steps.title: Contact your National Commission for UNESCO
application_steps.detail: Ask your country's National Commission for UNESCO about its national procedure and pre-selection. Individuals and institutions cannot apply to UNESCO directly: only candidates endorsed by their National Commission are considered. For the 2026-2027 call the commissions asked for applications by 23 January 2026.

application_steps.title: Get a pre-admission document from a Chinese university
application_steps.detail: Every candidate must hold a pre-admission notice or an invitation letter from a designated Chinese university or professor. Check the host university's own admission requirements for academic ability and language. The China Scholarship Council university page shows available fields.

application_steps.title: Register online in the Chinese Government Scholarship system
application_steps.detail: Submit the online application with Type A Application and agency number 00001, so that UNESCO appears as the sponsor, and upload all supporting documents. Applications without this online registration are not considered, and the application form for the National Commission can only be downloaded after it.

application_steps.title: National Commission nominates you to UNESCO
application_steps.detail: After national pre-selection, the National Commission emails its nomination letter, the application form and all documents to UNESCO by 10 February 2026 (2026-2027 call). Each invited Member State may nominate at most two candidates, and one of them must be a woman.

application_steps.title: UNESCO screening and Chinese selection
application_steps.detail: UNESCO screens applications from 11 February to 2 March 2026. The concerned Chinese universities then select, from March to June 2026, and the Chinese authorities and UNESCO approve, with attention to gender equality and diversity. Academic qualifications and the eligibility criteria are the main screening factors, and host institutions may also look at extracurricular activities.

application_steps.title: Results through the National Commission
application_steps.detail: UNESCO informs the National Commissions of the selected fellows, and the fellowships are awarded in late June to early July 2026. A candidate who has not received a result by 15 August 2026 should treat the application as rejected.

application_steps.title: Get a visa and start the fellowship
application_steps.detail: Fellows obtain their visa from the Chinese embassy or consulate in their country before leaving, at their own cost. The fellowship starts in late August to early September 2026, and the academic year 2026-2027 ends on 15 July 2027. Fellows enrol full-time in the programme they are admitted to.

application_steps.title: No renewal under this programme
application_steps.detail: The fellowship cannot be extended or renewed, and a repeated award under the same UNESCO programme is not allowed. A fellow may stay on in China with other funding, such as another China Scholarship Council award or an outside sponsor, and should ask the host university and CSC early if more years are needed.
